developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_encryption_at_rest_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-11 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_firewall_whitelist_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-12 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo SSH Keys"]
      requirement["Civo SSH Keys: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0681"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-keys", label: "Civo SSH Keys", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_least_privilege_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-1 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_automated_backups_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-2 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo SSH Keys"]
      requirement["Civo SSH Keys: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0683"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-keys", label: "Civo SSH Keys", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_pod_security_restricted_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-3 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-4 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.

civo apikey current
aws configure list

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_keys.civo_keys_encryption_at_rest_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo SSH Keys: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-7 SSH Key Management & Bastion Access)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo SSH Keys configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo keys list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo SSH Keys"]
      requirement["Civo SSH Keys: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0688"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-keys", label: "Civo SSH Keys", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application encryption and secret access
developer_guide.contract: Key or secret identifier, version, encryption context and permitted operations
dependencies: An existing key or secret and an application identity
Explicit cryptographic or secret-read permissions
steps: Choose the supported key or secret API and the narrowest grant.
Keep credentials and plaintext key material out of source and logs.
Define version selection, rotation and error handling in the application.
tests: Encrypt and decrypt, or read the expected secret version.
Reject an unauthorized identity and an incorrect key or encryption context.
failures: Access denied: check both caller permissions and key or secret policy.
Decryption error: verify key version, context and ciphertext format.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_tls_enforcement_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-1 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_encryption_at_rest_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-3 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_firewall_whitelist_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-4 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_least_privilege_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-5 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-autoscaling", label: "Civo Auto-Scaler", h: 64, pos: "b" }

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_automated_backups_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-6 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_pod_security_restricted_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-7 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-8 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Auto-Scaler"]
      requirement["Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0696"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-autoscaling", label: "Civo Auto-Scaler", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_encryption_at_rest_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-11 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Auto-Scaler"]
      requirement["Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0699"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-autoscaling", label: "Civo Auto-Scaler", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_firewall_whitelist_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-12 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_least_privilege_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-1 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_automated_backups_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-2 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Auto-Scaler"]
      requirement["Civo Auto-Scaler: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0702"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-autoscaling", label: "Civo Auto-Scaler", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_pod_security_restricted_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-3 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-4 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

flowchart TB

      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end

developer_guide.name: HTTP application with a managed backend
developer_guide.contract: Listener port, application port, health endpoint and shutdown grace period
dependencies: An application artifact and a supported compute runtime
A configured listener or load balancer
A database or API endpoint and a runtime identity
steps: Deploy the artifact and configure environment variables and identity.
Connect listener routing to the actual application port.
Configure readiness, timeouts and graceful shutdown before shifting traffic.
tests: Call the health route and a real application route.
Replace one instance and verify traffic is drained without failed writes.
failures: 502/503: verify target health, listening address and backend port.
Backend failure: check connection limits, credentials and outbound reachability.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_autoscaling.civo_autoscaling_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Cluster Node Auto-Scaling Pools)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Auto-Scaler configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo autoscaling list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Auto-Scaler"]
      requirement["Civo Auto-Scaler: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0705"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-autoscaling", label: "Civo Auto-Scaler", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end
