developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_least_privilege_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-5 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_automated_backups_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-6 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Deep Lake"]
      requirement["Civo Deep Lake: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0976"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-deep-lake", label: "Civo Deep Lake", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.

failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_pod_security_restricted_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-7 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path
Verify resource scope, service support, and the actual policy effect before deployment.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-8 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Deep Lake"]
      requirement["Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0979"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-deep-lake", label: "Civo Deep Lake", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_encryption_at_rest_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-11 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_firewall_whitelist_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-12 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Deep Lake"]
      requirement["Civo Deep Lake: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0982"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-deep-lake", label: "Civo Deep Lake", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_least_privilege_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-1 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_automated_backups_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-2 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

civo apikey current
aws configure list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile)

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_pod_security_restricted_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-3 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Deep Lake"]
      requirement["Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile)"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0985"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-deep-lake", label: "Civo Deep Lake", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-4 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Application model invocation
developer_guide.contract: Model ID, validated input schema, output schema, timeout and token budget
dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_tls_enforcement_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-5 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

dependencies: A deployed or available model endpoint and invocation permission
Application validation, rate limits and an explicit data-handling policy
steps: Configure model selection, identity and bounded inference settings.
Validate inputs and minimize sensitive data sent to the model.
Validate output before using it in application decisions or tool calls.
tests: Exercise malformed input, timeout, quota exhaustion and unexpected output.
Verify model output cannot bypass application authorization.
failures: 429: inspect model quota and request concurrency.
Invalid output: enforce schema validation and bounded retry or fallback.

checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_private_networking_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-6 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Deep Lake"]
      requirement["Civo Deep Lake: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0988"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-deep-lake", label: "Civo Deep Lake", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_deep_lake.civo_deep_lake_encryption_at_rest_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Deep Lake: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-7 Deep Lake AI Vector Database)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Deep Lake configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo deep list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_tls_enforcement_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-1 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_private_networking_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-2 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Compliance Controls"]
      requirement["Civo Compliance Controls: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0991"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-compliance", label: "Civo Compliance Controls", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

civo apikey current
aws configure list

checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_encryption_at_rest_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-3 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_firewall_whitelist_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-4 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_least_privilege_t5

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-5 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

    end

      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}

      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0994"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-compliance", label: "Civo Compliance Controls", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]

      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_automated_backups_t6

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-6 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-0995"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-compliance", label: "Civo Compliance Controls", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets"]

      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_pod_security_restricted_t7

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-7 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_audit_telemetry_t8

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-8 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_tls_enforcement_t9

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Encrypted Transport with TLS 1.3 Termination (Tier-9 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_loadbalancer"
  not r.change.after.tls_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce tls_enabled for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test protocol negotiation and certificate trust
Transport encryption, identity validation, and authorization are separate checks. A SecureTransport condition alone does not set a minimum TLS version.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_private_networking_t10

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Require Private Network Attachment without Public IP (Tier-10 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_instance"
  not r.change.after.network_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce network_id for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

civo apikey current
aws configure list

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_encryption_at_rest_t11

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest (Tier-11 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Denial of Service: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_object_store"
  not r.change.after.encryption_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce encryption_enabled for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Compliance Controls"]
      requirement["Civo Compliance Controls: Mandate AES-256 Server-Side Encryption at Rest"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-1000"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-compliance", label: "Civo Compliance Controls", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Verify key identity and permitted encrypt or decrypt operations
Check service support, key location, key policy, and the service identity. Encryption at rest does not prevent an authorized data read.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_firewall_whitelist_t12

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Restrict Ingress to Zero-Trust CIDR Whitelists (Tier-12 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Elevation of Privilege: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_firewall"
  not r.change.after.firewall_id
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce firewall_id for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test an allowed source and a denied source against the actual endpoint
Identity, network reachability, and application permissions are independent. Private networking and DNS require explicit service-specific configuration.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_least_privilege_t1

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Role-Based Ephemeral Scoped API Tokens (Tier-1 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: SOC 2 Type II CC6.1, ISO/IEC 27001 A.13.1, NIST CSF PR.AC-3, PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 1
# Threat Vector: Spoofing: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_iam_token"
  not r.change.after.permissions
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce permissions for compliance standard SOC 2 Type II CC6.1", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Test the intended principal and a principal outside the allowed scope
Evaluate effective permissions, inherited grants, explicit denies, and credential lifetime. A policy attachment alone does not establish least privilege.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_automated_backups_t2

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enable Daily Automated Snapshots and Backups (Tier-2 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0, SOC 2 CC6.6, ISO 27001 A.12.6, NIST 800-53 SC-7
# Threat Vector: Tampering: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_volume"
  not r.change.after.backup_enabled
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce backup_enabled for compliance standard CIS Civo Kubernetes Benchmark v1.0", [r.address])
}

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Perform restore or failover verification with recorded recovery targets
Replication, versioning, retention lock, and backup recovery provide different guarantees. Select supported settings and test recovery before relying on them.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

threat_model.attack_vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
threat_model.defense_barrier: Civo Firewall CIDR Ingress Whitelist & Enforced Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile)

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_pod_security_restricted_t3

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile) (Tier-3 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1), SOC 2 CC6.7, NIST SP 800-53 SC-8, PCI DSS Requirement 4
# Threat Vector: Repudiation: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_kubernetes_cluster"
  not r.change.after.applications
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce applications for compliance standard HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(1)", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan
deployment_mermaid:
flowchart TB
    subgraph proposal["Civo Cloud: proposed control change"]
      change["Proposed configuration for Civo Compliance Controls"]
      requirement["Civo Compliance Controls: Enforce Pod Security Standards (Restricted Profile)"]
      identity@{ icon: "logos:civo-iam", label: "Civo API key or team permissions", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      change --> requirement
      identity -.->|Required permissions| change
    end
    subgraph validation["Review and pre-deployment validation"]
      check{"Service-specific checks pass?"}
      reject["Revise configuration; no change applied"]
      review["Owner review: CIVO-BP-1004"]
      requirement --> check
      check -->|No or unknown| reject
      check -->|Yes| review
    end
    subgraph target["Civo Cloud: resource administration"]
      resource@{ icon: "logos:civo-compliance", label: "Civo Compliance Controls", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      review -->|Apply through the supported service management API| resource
    end
    subgraph verification["Readback and operational evidence"]
      verify["Read back the effective setting and exercise its rejection path"]
      evidence@{ icon: "logos:civo-audit", label: "Civo audit events and cluster telemetry", h: 64, pos: "b" }
      outcome{"Observed behavior matches control?"}
      followup["Investigate drift or missing enforcement"]
      accepted["Record resource scope, result, and evidence"]
      resource -->|Read effective configuration| verify
      resource -.->|Separate audit or evidence path| evidence
      verify --> outcome
      outcome -->|No or unknown| followup
      outcome -->|Yes| accepted
      evidence -.->|Correlate with test results| accepted
    end

dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.

aws configure list

Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.

opa_policy:
package civo.civo_compliance.civo_compliance_audit_telemetry_t4

default allow = false

# Rule: Civo Compliance Controls: Mandate Real-Time Audit Log Forwarding to SIEM (Tier-4 CIS Benchmark & SOC 2 Hardening)
# Compliance: CIS Critical Security Controls v8, NIST 800-53 CP-9, HITRUST CSF v9.4, GDPR Article 32
# Threat Vector: Information Disclosure: Unauthorized exploit targeting unhardened Civo Compliance Controls configuration
deny[msg] {
  r := input.resource_changes[_]
  r.type == "civo_network"
  not r.change.after.audit_logging
  msg := sprintf("Civo resource %v must enforce audit_logging for compliance standard CIS Critical Security Controls v8", [r.address])
}
remediation: Inspect resource via Civo CLI: civo compliance list or apply Terraform: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform apply tfplan

developer_guide.name: Finding ingestion and bounded response
developer_guide.contract: Finding ID, resource, severity, status and deduplication key
dependencies: Enabled detectors or explicitly connected telemetry sources
A finding destination and a separately authorized response handler
steps: Enable the supported detectors and connect their sources.
Route a test finding to the response handler.
Require idempotency and authorization before any resource mutation.
tests: Deliver a known finding and confirm it reaches the right owner.
Replay the event and confirm duplicate handling is safe.
failures: Missing finding: check detector availability and source enablement.
Repeated remediation: inspect event deduplication and handler state.
developer_guide.diagnostics:
civo apikey current
aws configure list
developer_guide.scope: Reference integration pattern. Provision and configure the named dependencies separately; the companion catalog snippets are not a complete application deployment.

diagram_details.scope: Control deployment and verification workflow. Companion policy and configuration snippets are illustrative; validate their schema, inputs, and resource coverage before applying them.
checks: Generate a known event and verify delivery to the configured destination
Telemetry requires enabled sources, access permissions, retention, and a tested delivery path. A detection or alert does not automatically remediate a resource.
Confirm effective permissions and record both successful and rejected test cases.
